clue.text: Area in which rash Scots might go astray

indicators.note: letters that go astray wander out of their order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stretch of countryside where reckless Scotsmen are liable to lose their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might go astray' rearranges RASH SCOTS. The Trossachs are a wooded, hilly area of central Scotland, so the anagram fodder fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trossachs is a named region of the Scottish highlands, so it is an example of a geographical area.

clue.text: Work hard, say, for various courses

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word aloud and take its sound-alike

parts.note: to tax someone is to work them hard, strain them

explanation.surface: A tip for getting through a varied set of lessons: put in plenty of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals a sound-alike: TAX said aloud gives TACKS. 'Courses' looks like academic study; here it is sailing, where tacks are the zigzag headings a boat takes into the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing, a tack is a course steered at an angle to the wind, so tacks are several different courses.

clue.text: Side with head giving old pupil lines

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
verse is written in lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Siding with the headmaster earns a former pupil some lines as punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests a headteacher, fitting 'old pupil' and 'lines' (a school punishment), but it is the head on a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse of a coin or medal is the face bearing the principal design, typically a monarch's portrait.

clue.text: Rack for putting case on

explanation.surface: A frame on which a box is placed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack stretches its victim, so a torturer's rack is literally a stretching device; a medical case, an injured patient, is carried lying on a stretcher.

clue.text: Villain reformed. OK at a pinch? Nothing in it

indicators.note: in it tells us the zero goes inside the rearranged letters
something reformed has been made over into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer has turned over a new leaf, but only up to a point, with nothing inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Villain reformed' reads as a criminal gone straight, but 'reformed' is the anagram signal for the next four words, and 'in it' is the container signal for the zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The pirate captain with a hook for a hand is the chief bad guy of Barrie's Peter Pan.

clue.text: Relative security is basically restricted to leaders

indicators.note: only the leading letter of each of the three words is kept

explanation.surface: A statement that family safety comes down, at root, to whoever is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted to leaders' keeps only the initial letters of 'security is basically'. Sib is an old word for a brother or sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Sib is short for sibling, a brother or sister, or more broadly a kinsman.

clue.text: Feeble light in which animal's heard, but not seen

indicators.note: heard means we listen for a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the tapir is a hoofed animal with a short trunk

explanation.surface: A dim glow by which a creature can be heard but not seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' signals a sound-alike: TAPIR said aloud gives TAPER. 'but not seen' adds the surface joke: you hear the beast but see only a thin candle.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a slender candle or wax-coated wick giving only a weak flame.

clue.text: Singer getting half of score, or exact copy

parts.note: a score is twenty, half of which is ten
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vocalist earns ten points out of twenty, or makes a perfect imitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exact copy' is a second definition: in law the tenor of a document can mean an exact transcript of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with the highest natural adult voice in the usual range.

clue.text: Seabird found in transatlantic vessel, note

parts.note: the Pinta was one of the three ships Columbus took across the Atlantic in 1492
do is the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A bird of the ocean spotted aboard a ship crossing the Atlantic, with a note about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pinta sailed with the Nina and the Santa Maria. 'found in' is a link: nothing goes inside anything.
explanation.definitionFit: The pintado petrel, or Cape pigeon, is a chequered southern ocean bird.

clue.text: Start off term as political leader in the house

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off the front of the word

parts.note: a presidency is the period a president holds office

explanation.surface: A new president begins a stint as leader of the legislative chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' removes the opening P from PRESIDENCY. 'the house' suggests a parliament, but the definition means simply being in residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Residency is the state of living somewhere, so to be in residence is to be at home in the building.

clue.text: Attempt to conceal deliveries in vessel

indicators.note: in places the deliveries inside the vessel

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hide parcels inside a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. An over is a cricket term: a bowler's set of six balls, so 'deliveries' is not post.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover-up is a campaign of concealment, especially of wrongdoing by those in power.

clue.text: Fruit bats

explanation.surface: A note on fruit-eating flying mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas are a tropical fruit; bats is slang for crazy, as is bananas.

clue.text: A little fish for man avoiding fat

explanation.surface: A small piece of fish suits someone staying off fatty foods.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Sprat is the nursery-rhyme man who 'could eat no fat', while his wife could eat no lean.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a small herring-like sea fish; Jack Sprat of the nursery rhyme famously would eat no fat.

clue.text: Character on typewriter impedes writing for Cockney

indicators.note: a London Cockney drops the H sound, so the H is removed from each word

parts.note: hampers means hinders or impedes
hand means handwriting, someone's writing

explanation.surface: A typist's keyboard symbol gets in the way of a Londoner's penmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Cockney' drops each H, as the Cockney accent of East London does: HAMPERS becomes AMPERS and HAND becomes AND.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampersand is the printed symbol for 'and', found on typewriter keyboards.

clue.text: Mrs Whistler, for example, spotted insect

explanation.surface: The artist's wife is likened to a speckled bug.
explanation.walkthrough: Whistler's famous portrait of his mother means she was a woman put on canvas; the painted lady is also an orange-and-black spotted butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistler's mother is a woman depicted on canvas; the painted lady is a migratory butterfly with dappled wings.

clue.text: Whisky or port

explanation.surface: A spirit or a fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink, fitting 'whisky', but it is a harbour town: Rye in Sussex was one of England's Cinque Ports.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a whiskey distilled mainly from rye grain; Rye in East Sussex is an old harbour town.

clue.text: Fancy entering tavern to get put out again!

indicators.note: entering places one word inside the other

parts.note: to fancy something is to relish it
a pub is a tavern

explanation.surface: Fancy going into a bar only to be thrown out again!
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' is the container signal. 'put out' suggests being ejected from the bar, but it means issued in print.
explanation.definitionFit: To republish is to issue a book or article a second time, putting it out once more.

clue.text: Instrument sounded behind 28

parts.note: 28 across is a bat called a fox; taken as the ordinary fox, the brass instrument blown by riders chasing it fits

explanation.surface: A musical instrument played behind the bat at 28.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to FLYING FOX; read 28 as the plain fox pursued by mounted hunters, and the instrument blown behind it follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the brass horn sounded by riders following hounds as they chase a fox.

clue.text: See large bird on crag fly off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Look: a big raptor perched on a rocky outcrop takes wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges ON CRAG FLY. 'fly off' reads as the bird taking flight, a natural picture of a raptor.
explanation.definitionFit: The gyrfalcon is the biggest falcon, an Arctic hunting bird of prey.

clue.text: Prayer that's uplifting for lots of people

definitions.text: that's uplifting for lots of people

explanation.surface: Prayer described as raising the spirits of many.
explanation.walkthrough: A paternoster is also a lift of open cars moving continuously, carrying many people up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord's Prayer is named from its opening Latin words; a continuously moving open elevator carries passengers up in a stream.

clue.text: Economical fee taken back from £3.50?

indicators.note: taken from tells us to remove letters from the spelt-out sum

parts.note: three pounds fifty is written out as three fifty

indicators.note: back means the word for a charge is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheap charge is refunded out of a small sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns FEE into EEF, and 'taken ... from' removes those letters in order from THREE FIFTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thrifty is careful with money, spending sparingly.

clue.text: Extremely chary about love?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the zero goes inside
extremely asks for the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scores, the letter O

explanation.surface: Being very wary in matters of the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'chary', C and Y, and 'about' places O (love) between them. The whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coy person is bashful or reticent, especially in romance.

clue.text: Capital eccentric person provided? Fine

parts.note: a card is a comic or eccentric character
provided means if
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: An odd character in the capital, if things are fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

clue.text: Soundly criticized in military quarters

explanation.surface: Loudly condemned within an army camp.
explanation.walkthrough: To barrack is to jeer noisily, as cricket crowds do; troops quartered in barracks were barracked.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracking is noisy jeering; soldiers housed in a barrack block were barracked.

clue.text: Priest performing song in audition first

indicators.note: first puts the song before the other word
an audition is a hearing, so we take the word as it sounds

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
an actor performing is on stage

explanation.surface: A clergyman sings a song as he tries out for a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in audition' says the song is taken by its sound, and 'first' puts it ahead. Aaron, brother of Moses, was the first high priest of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Aaron was Moses's brother and the first high priest of the Israelites.

clue.text: A legal process unfinished in courts

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a trial is a legal process

explanation.surface: A lawsuit left incomplete in the law courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts the L from TRIAL. 'courts' are not law courts but courtyards: atria are open central halls.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is a central open hall or courtyard, so atria are its plural, inner courtyards.

clue.text: Covering ten with queen may be appropriate

indicators.note: covering in a down clue puts one piece on top of the other

parts.note: Anne was a queen of Great Britain
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A monarch may be fit to cover a tenner.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'Covering' puts ANNE above X. 'appropriate' is the verb, to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex territory is to seize it and take it as one's own.

clue.text: Deduce there's no poem of this name

parts.note: to deduce is to infer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Conclude that no poem bears this title.
explanation.walkthrough: Dante's Inferno is the first part of the Divine Comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferno is the title of the first part of Dante's Divine Comedy, an epic in verse.

clue.text: Right away

explanation.surface: Agreeing, then leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Off means right as in the off side of a horse or vehicle, its right-hand side; off also means away, departed.
explanation.definitionFit: The off side of a horse or car is its right-hand side; to be off is to be gone or absent.

clue.text: Leaving a lot to be desired, whenever it's unsuccessful?

definitions.text: Leaving a lot to be desired, whenever it's unsuccessful?

parts.words: Leaving a lot to be desired, whenever it's unsuccessful?
parts.note: the phrase for something disappointing is read literally: a lot, an item for sale, is left unsold when bidding fails

explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' is a numbered item at a sale; when nobody bids enough it is left, still wanted by its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: At a sale by bidding, an unsold lot remains with the seller, who still wants a buyer.

clue.text: Composer's dance study lacking middle section

definitions.note: the possessive 's here stands for 'is' and joins the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a hay is an old country dance

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A musician's dance piece was studied without its middle movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking middle section' drops the E from DEN. The 's in 'Composer's' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was an Austrian composer of the classical period.

clue.text: In a hurry to stain a bat

parts.note: flying means moving very fast, rushing
to fox paper is to discolour it with brown spots

explanation.surface: Rushing to put a mark on a cricket bat.
explanation.walkthrough: Foxing is the brown spotting on old book pages. 'bat' suggests a cricket bat, but the definition is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The flying fox is a large fruit-eating bat with a fox-like face.
